tasks.instructions: Experiment E1 (tests H30): New lineage E: CUTLASS sm100 builder GEMMs with EVT fusion and TF32 operands straight from fp32 memory for the six wide-C small-image rows. Build from scratch (you may read only the r0 anchor and the lineage conclusions; do not read lineage A/B/D code). Target rows: 2,768,7,7; 8,768,7,7; 16,768,7,7; 32,768,7,7; 8,384,14,14; 16,384,14,14. All other rows run the r0 anchor path unchanged (the operator merges per workload). Language 'cutlass' (C++; two files: kernel.cu with no torch headers plus binding.cpp; CUTLASS 4.4.1 headers at $CUTLASS_DIR/include; target_hardware [B200] only, since tcgen05 code does not build for plain sm_100). Pipeline per call, 4-5 launches: (K1) your own bulk-plane depthwise conv for 7x7/14x14 images: 1-D cp.async.bulk of channel-plane groups into zero-padded smem, one thread per 7-output row segment, plus the dwconv bias; write d as fp32 TOKEN-MAJOR [b][hw][C] (tcgen05 kind::tf32 needs K-major A and B), per-token LN partial sums (sum, sumsq) via atomics or per-group partials finalised as mu[token], rstd[token]; spare CTAs compute the fold vectors u[n] = sum_c W1[n][c]*lnw[c], v[n] = sum_c W1[n][c]*lnb[c] + b1[n] and b2'[c] = sum_k W2[c][k]*gb[k] + b2[c] (coalesced 16-B loads, all loads issued before use, compile-time trip counts). No weight conversion in the first build: both GEMMs use TF32. (G1) CUTLASS CollectiveBuilder, arch Sm100, KernelTmaWarpSpecialized1SmSm100 (or 2Sm where the tile allows), batched L = B images, M = HW (49 or 196, tile M = 64 or 128), N = 4C, K = C; ElementA = ElementB = cutlass::tfloat32_t on the fp32 d and fp32 W1 (verify in step 1 that the resulting TMA descriptor uses the TFLOAT32 data type: compare one tile's accumulator against an fp64 reference of round-to-nearest TF32 operands and against truncation; the bit pattern must match RNE, H14). EVT epilogue: Sm90RowBroadcast(rstd, mu with batch stride), Sm90ColBroadcast(u, v), compute z = rstd*(acc - mu*u) + v, cutlass::epilogue::thread::GELU (the erf form, NOT GELU_taylor), store the hidden (fp32 for the TF32 rows, [b][hw][4C] K-major for GEMM2) and Sm90ColReduction of z*z over M per batch into gf2[b][k] (atomic across M tiles where M > tile). If the sm100 epilogue cannot instantiate the ColReduction, fall back to an AuxStore of the hidden and compute the per-image sumsq in K3 with a cluster of 8 CTAs per image exchanging the 4C partials through DSMEM. (K3) one-round GRN scale kernel: grid (image, k-slice), each CTA reads gf2[b][:] (12 KB), computes gf = sqrt, mean_k, s_b[k] = 1 + gw[k]*gf/(mean+eps), then rescales its hidden slice in place with all loads issued before any store; nothing else is chained. (G2) CUTLASS batched: A = W2 [C][4C] (tf32, batch stride 0), B = scaled hidden [hw][4C] per image (K-major, N = HW), D[b][c][hw] with batch stride C*HW = NCHW directly, source C = x (beta = 1) and per-row bias b2'. The CTA count is tiny at 7x7 (6*B tiles), so use split-K: first try the sm100 stream-K/split-K scheduler; if it is not available in 4.4.1, run batched over (image, k-split) with fp32 partials [B*KS][C][HW] and a one-round reduce+residual kernel (coalesced, all loads first). Steps: (0) time the r0 anchor interleaved x3 as the in-session control; (1) compile gate with no GPU needed first: G1 and G2 instantiations for 49x3072x768 (L=8) and 196x1536x384 (L=8), record nvcc wall time (abort the design if two instantiations exceed 200 s: the portal limit is 300 s), registers, smem, spills; then the H14 bit check; (2) time G1 cold (after a 2xL2 zero-fill) at 8,768 and 8,384 and compare with the leader-implied budget: kill the EVT route if G1 alone exceeds 14 us at 8,768 (that is cuBLASLt GEMM1 + K2 on lineage A); (3) full pipeline, run_tests 16/16 x 10 rounds with the portal-order check; (4) precision log on the six rows: 10 seeded rounds (seed 200) vs an fp64 reference, per row max |err| and count beyond atol + 1e-5|ref| (TF32 RNE is the same 10-bit mantissa as fp16, so expect max about 2.4e-3 at 32,768; any beyond-atol element switches that row's activation operand to an fp16 hi/lo split or fp32 SIMT); (5) per-launch cold breakdown (harness_time) of K1/G1/K3/G2 on 8,768 and 8,384, and if GEMM2 is ingest-bound at low CTA counts (H31), raise KS. Report every finding with its source, including compile times and which EVT nodes instantiated. Success: run_tests 16/16; the six target rows at or under 2,768 32 / 8,768 38 / 8,384 42 / 16,384 58 / 16,768 50 / 32,768 68 us rented on at least 4 of 6 rows, with the parent-equivalent merge rows timed in the same container (operator-provided numbers: A r4 48.5 / 44.4 / 50.4 / 71.5 / 53.2 / 70.1, D r4 32.4 at 2,768); CUTLASS build time under 200 s; precision log delivered with 0 beyond-atol elements. Refuted if: G1 with the EVT epilogue runs slower cold than 14 us at 8,768 or 12 us at 8,384 (then the library epilogue is no cheaper than cuBLASLt + K2), or the per-batch column reduction and the split-K GEMM2 both fail to instantiate on sm100 and the fallbacks push the six rows above A's times, or the build exceeds 200 s. This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules for the CUTLASS route): (1) no PDL anywhere: launch every CUTLASS kernel without programmatic dependent launch (GemmUniversalAdapter::run / operator() with launch_with_pdl left false; never set cudaLaunchAttributeProgrammaticStreamSerialization). (2) Call the adapter's initialize() (or to_underlying_arguments) with this call's pointers on every call: its params embed TMA descriptors, which must be encoded per call; cache only shape-keyed configuration, never an initialised Gemm object or converted data. (3) The CUTLASS workspace and every atomic accumulator (gf2, LN partials, split-K partials) come from torch.empty inside run(), which is uninitialised: zero them with your own kernel or cudaMemsetAsync on the current stream in every call before use. (4) Spec language may be 'cutlass' or 'cuda_cpp' (both compile the same way); keep ld_flags you need (e.g. -lcuda).

Experiment E2 (tests H29): Lineage A lean passes: K2 at stream rate, W2 conversion split over warps, and the owed 10-round precision log. Parent: r4-a-e1-bulkplane-wprep (lineage A's best). Step 0 (hard deliverable, do first): precision log for the parent as shipped, all 16 rows, the harness's 10 seeded rounds (seed 200) against an fp64 reference: per row the max |err| and the count of elements beyond that row's own atol (workload.jsonl) + 1e-5|ref|. If any row has a beyond-atol element, switch its hidden or W2 operand to a hi/lo fp16 split (2 cuBLASLt GEMMs accumulated, or hi/lo columns) and re-log. Step 1 (critic's probe, H29): time K2 alone after the 2xL2 zero-fill at 64,96 / 32,128 / 8,320 against a plain read+write copy kernel of the same fp16 bytes (616 / 134 / 21 MB), interleaved x3; record the copy rate in TB/s. Step 2: rewrite K2 (GELU + GRN sum of squares over the fp16 hidden) as a stream-rate kernel: 256-thread CTAs, each CTA owns a long token run of ONE image (thousands of tokens at 64,96; the whole image at small rows), each thread fixed on 8 hidden channels (one uint4), 8 uint4 loads in flight before the first erff, exact erff kept (a custom erf only if it is at least 1.3x faster AND |err| <= 2e-7 vs erff over [-10,10]), sumsq accumulated in registers across the run, one float4 atomic pair per 8 channels per CTA into the 4-copy accumulators, bias b1 folded as now. Try evict_last on the hidden stores for rows whose hidden is <= 42 MB and evict_first above; keep whichever wins per row class. Keep the kernel sequence identical on every call. Step 3: the W2 conversion in K1 (rows with the hidden > 16 MB: B >= 8 at C=768, B = 16 at C=384) is one warp per W2 row with 4 serial 768-column rounds: split each row over 4 warps with a CTA-level reduction and 16-B loads, all loads issued before use; target weights-only K1 <= 6 us at C=768 (now 8.9-11), measured with the conv-only / weights-only / both ablation at 2,768, 8,768, 16,768. Step 4: run_tests 16/16 x 10 rounds with the parent interleaved x3 in the same container as the control, and the r0 anchor once for the ratio; report per-row rented deltas, not band means. Step 5 (optional if time remains): the nwmin 4 vs 8 interleaved comparison left open in r4. Report findings with sources; a session that ends without the step 0 log returns no candidate. Success: K2 at 64,96 <= 260 us rented (from 447), 32,128 <= 65 (from 113), 8,320 <= 22 (from 38), so the full rows reach 64,96 <= 960, 32,128 <= 245, 8,320 <= 75 rented against the parent in the same container; weights-only K1 <= 6 us at C=768 with 8,768 and 16,768 gaining >= 3 us; precision log delivered with 0 beyond-atol elements on all 16 rows (or the hi/lo fix applied where needed). Refuted if: The copy probe shows the parent's K2 already at >= 80% of the copy kernel's rate at 64,96 (then the kernel is SIMT-bound and only a cheaper erf helps), or the rewritten K2 is within 15% of the old one at 64,96 and 32,128 in the same container. If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds.
